title: Column sensitivity: a column that holds a person's data is found by its name and the shape of its values, and reaches a model by name only
request: Phase 1's sensitivity gap: nothing told which columns hold a person's data, so example values, category names and top values of an e-mail or a phone column reached the profile, the Home analysis and the intern's description. Classes pii, sensitive and restricted from name tokens and value shapes, never keeping a value; a personal column reaches a model by name only and a dataset never holds its values; adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.sensitivity (classify, of_name, of_values with the Luhn check, strip); ColumnCard.sensitivity and sensitivity_why (data card v3); the profile keeps no preview and the Home analysis no top values, histogram or range for such a column; the intern's describe_data names the class and gives no example; data.analysed carries the column-to-class map (event v7); Home's analysis card lists them; the data-limit tests plant personal columns and require that no purpose sees a value.
plan: The rules in dclab_core: restricted (secrets, card numbers by Luhn, national ids, IBANs), pii, sensitive, none; a count, flag or rate about such data is not that data.
Put the class on the column card and strip what carries values at the source, so every caller is protected.
The same at the profile and the Home analysis, which are what the models and the UI read.
Carry the class in the event and show it on Home.
Prove it with tests that plant personal values in every table the callers read and look for them in every prompt.

decisions.decision: Strip at the source (the card, the profile, the analysis) rather than at each model call.
decisions.why: A fix at each caller would miss the next one; the data-limit tests then check the callers.

decisions.decision: pii and restricted lose their whole distribution; sensitive keeps it but no category name or example.
decisions.why: A phone number's quantiles are a number someone could be called on; a diagnosis' shares are a statistic.

decisions.decision: A count, flag or rate about a kind of data is not that data (email_opens, has_phone, phone_type).
decisions.why: Marking them would blind the tools to ordinary features for no protection.

decisions.decision: A bare 'name' column, and name with a person word (customer, patient, member), is pii; product_name is not.
decisions.why: The entity's own name is the common case; qualified names of things are not people.

decisions.decision: The event carries the map of column to class, as meta.
decisions.why: Names are already in the event; the class lets a later reader know why a column has no values.

change: dclab_core sensitivity.py (new), datacard.py (ColumnCard fields, v3, column_card), experience.py (data.analysed field), CHANGELOG 0.44.0, schemas; dclab_rnd studio/data.py (profile), draft/analyze.py, intern/tools.py, experience/hooks.py, web home.html; tests test_sensitivity.py (new), test_model_data_limits.py (PersonalDataTests), the version pins; CORE_INTEGRATION.md, the plan.

findings.defect: The first name rules read email_opens as an e-mail column and date_of_birth as nothing.
findings.scenario: A churn table's email_opens count lost its quantiles; a date_of_birth column kept its values.
findings.cause: Adjacent-pair matching and no notion of a column that is about a kind of data.
findings.fix: A set of 'about' words (count, flag, rate, opens, type...) and small words dropped before pairing.

findings.defect: The Home analysis and the profile were the real carriers of values (top values, histogram, previews), not only the data card.
findings.scenario: A card-only fix would have left the intern's describe_data and the Home agent's get_profile seeing three emails per column.
findings.cause: Three different descriptions of a column in three modules.
findings.fix: strip() is applied in column_card, profile_table and the analysis; one rule for what carries a value.

findings.defect: The name rules missed common spellings: phone_num, phone1, email1, card_no, cc_num, account_no, postal_code, fname, lname.
findings.scenario: A phone_num column with plain digits kept its examples in describe_data; a postal_code the same.
findings.cause: num was read as 'number of' (about), digit-suffixed names did not tokenise, and the pairs listed only the long forms.
findings.fix: Trailing digits dropped from tokens, num no longer 'about', the short forms of the card and account pairs, postal, fname, lname and msisdn added.

findings.defect: The value shapes missed real forms: a card or phone column made float by a missing row (a sixteen-digit card number written with a trailing .0), a column mixing e-mails and phones, placeholders diluting the share, a sorted file, lowercase IBANs and IPv6.
findings.scenario: A 300-row cc_num column with NaNs had class none, and its previews, category names and range reached the profile, the card and the analysis.
findings.cause: One 60% threshold for every shape, the first 200 values only, no normalisation.
findings.fix: Floats written as whole numbers read as numbers, placeholders leave the share, an even sample across the column, a fifth of a column is enough for an e-mail, the shapes that mix count together, lowercase IBANs and IPv6 added.

findings.defect: Data written before 23.7 was never re-stripped: a stored profile kept its previews and a stored v1 or v2 card its category names and ranges, and an exported card took them as they were.
findings.scenario: describe_data on a project attached before the change returned three e-mail addresses as examples; the failure and workflow datasets carried an old card as stored.
findings.cause: The class was computed where a description is made, not where it is read or leaves.
findings.fix: upgrade_column and upgrade_card classify and strip any older description at the three boundaries: describe_data, DataCard.read for v1 and v2, anonymous_card.

findings.defect: False positives on the owner's own datasets: latitude and longitude of business places, PhoneService (yes/no), word_freq_mail, handle_time, race_time, orientation_deg.
findings.scenario: HyperAck's four coordinates lost their histogram, quantiles and previews.
findings.cause: Names read as personal without asking whether they are about the thing or the thing.
findings.fix: Coordinates are personal only as a home location; frequency, time, service, size, degrees and id words mark a column as about the data, not the data.

findings.defect: The levels of a sensitive column reached the final record as feature names (diagnosis=flu), and the Home note promised more than it did for the outcome column.
findings.scenario: top_final_features listed the 20 most important features by name.
findings.cause: The encoder names a level into a feature; the promise said 'never sent'.
findings.fix: Features named for a level of a personal column are left out of the final record; the Home note says the outcome you predict keeps its class names, since they define the task.

findings.defect: The per-purpose claim was under-tested and one existing test went vacuous.
findings.scenario: The Home-agent test passed before the change; PrivacyTest used a column named dob, now personal, so its range assertions were trivially true.
findings.cause: Tests written for the new behaviour only.
findings.fix: The leakage reviewer and the decision answerer are checked; the vacuous test uses a neutral column and a separate dob assertion.

findings.defect: Home's card listed only the 60 charted columns, cut at 12 with no count.
findings.scenario: A wide table's personal columns beyond the 60th were not named.
findings.cause: The list came from the charted columns.
findings.fix: From the whole profile, with 'and N more'.

findings.defect: The cleaning log quoted up to three values that failed to read as numbers or dates.
findings.scenario: A phone column read as numbers quoted '07911 123456' in the cleaning log shown on Home.
findings.cause: A helper that quotes failures, for any column.
findings.fix: Nothing is quoted for a column whose name or failures look personal.

findings.defect: The adoptability note asserted a main-product field that was never read.
findings.scenario: CORE_INTEGRATION said dataset_columns.sensitivity_class is the same four classes.
findings.cause: An expectation written as a fact.
findings.fix: FIELDS_MISSING names it as expected and unverified, and a test fails when the field lists gain it.

measurements.name: the rules over the owner's sample data
measurements.gate: no ordinary column of the project and public datasets is marked personal
measurements.result: 22 files of 12 datasets, 269 columns, 20,000 rows read of each: 1 column marked (adult.race, sensitive), the rest none
measurements.against_gate: 1 of 269 marked, and it is the one that is
limits: Names and shapes are heuristics; these datasets hold no e-mail, phone or card column to find.

outcome: A replica with an e-mail, a phone, a card number and a diagnosis column is marked, and no card, profile, analysis, event, synthetic table or prompt carries a value of them. Reviewed: 9 findings fixed.
lessons: Find every description of a column before fixing one: three modules each had their own carrier of values.
risks: Names and shapes are heuristics: a column of free text holding addresses is not caught by either.
The main product's dataset_columns.sensitivity_class is not in the field lists read; the mapping is described, not coded (23.12).
